A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with matching title, authors, core framework and retained experiments. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendix A report original synthetic-data measurements and model-finetuning results for mathematical reasoning and coding.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds experiments on downstream reasoning errors, mixed training data, training without gold answers and instruction following.

M1.justification: The sampling-budget rule, supervised-finetuning objective and model architectures remain unchanged. Section 8.1 adds procedural variants that retain all generated solutions or use LM-as-judge filtering instead of gold-answer filtering, extending the pipeline to training without gold labels.

E1.justification: v2 retains MATH, GSM-8K, Functional MATH and MBPP/HumanEval coverage. Section 8 adds a MATH scenario without access to gold training answers and a distinct instruction-following task using OpenAssistant1 prompts for synthetic training data and IFEval for evaluation.

E2.justification: Figure 10 adds mixed-source training as a comparator to training on exclusively WC or SE data. Section 8 also evaluates no-verification and LM-as-judge alternatives. The original Gemma/Gemini model pairs and human-solution baselines remain in the corresponding original experiments.

E3.justification: New protocols include allocating the sampling budget to 5 SE plus 15 WC solutions, evaluating unfiltered and model-filtered MATH data, and generating 1 Pro versus 35 Flash responses for 5,000 randomly selected OpenAssistant1 instructions with instruction-level IFEval evaluation. The original experiments' splits and training schedules are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds downstream false-positive analysis to test whether erroneous reasoning propagates through finetuning, a fixed-budget data-mixing ablation, and analyses of filtering and incorrect synthetic solutions without gold labels (Figures 7, 10 and 13–15). These substantially extend the retained dataset-size, sampling and coverage/diversity ablations.

E5.justification: Section 5.2 newly reports repeating the judge-based assessment of finetuned-model false-positive rates three times and averaging the results. This concerns repeated assessment, not evidence of repeated training runs. No confidence intervals or training-seed uncertainty reporting are added.

E6.justification: Original result plots are retained unchanged. New results report similar downstream false-positive rates, context-dependent benefits from mixed data, SE advantages for Gemma-generated data but WC advantages for Gemini-generated data without gold labels, and instruction-following gains, including a reported 12.8% relative IFEval gain for Gemma2-9B using Flash rather than Pro data. These are additional results under new conditions.

T1.justification: The coverage, diversity and false-positive definitions, finetuning objective and compute-matching derivation in Equation 1 are unchanged, including the equal-average-solution-length assumption. No new formal results or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims about WC-generated data outperforming SE-generated data at matched budgets and the weak-to-strong improvement contribution. These headline claims are not revised to incorporate the conditional findings from the added experiments.

C2.justification: v2 explains that benefits without gold labels depend on generator quality and finetuning setup, and offers noise and distribution-mixture explanations for failures. New Appendix A identifies unresolved success conditions and limits concerning iterative training, logit matching and verifier training. These substantially expand the earlier applicability discussion.

D1.justification: Sections 6 and 8 document new data-construction details, including mixture proportions and assigning Flash to verify WC outputs and Pro to verify SE outputs. Original decoding settings, batch sizes, training steps, checkpoint selection and learning-rate searches are retained and consolidated in Appendix G rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for OpenAssistant, Alpaca, LM-as-judge evaluation and IFEval. It removes the Srivastava et al. Functional MATH reference while retaining that benchmark. The broader positioning relative to STaR, weak-to-strong generalization and small-model sampling remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 tightens existing prose, moves detailed experimental settings into Appendix G, promotes ablations from Section 5.3 to Section 6 and reorders their discussion. It inserts the new experiments and discussion appendix, while most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Six substantive figures are added: downstream false-positive rates, data mixing, three figures on training without gold labels, and instruction following. Original plots and all five tables are retained with some relocation and renumbering. Takeaway boxes are also restyled with green backgrounds and rounded borders.

improvement.justification: v1 left important questions about downstream reasoning errors and dependence on gold-answer filtering untested. v2 directly investigates both through Figure 7 and Section 8, identifies conditions where WC data loses its advantage, and adds instruction-following evidence and explicit limitations. This substantially strengthens the paper's empirical scrutiny and applicability assessment. Unchanged broad headline claims and Section 10's stale statement that model-based verification remains future work weaken consistency, but do not outweigh these gains.
